note: Absolute ceilings for the headline metrics, enforced by compare.py
(--budgets) on top of the relative gate.  The relative gate alone cannot
stop slow drift: it compares HEAD against the latest tag only, and seven
release hops in five days at the maximum legal 15% each is 2.7x slower
with a green gate every time.  A breach fails the release even when the
relative gate passes, and [perf:accept] does not excuse it.
Bump ritual: raising a ceiling is a deliberate, reviewed edit to this
file, made in the same PR as the change that needs it, with the commit
message saying why the new ceiling is acceptable.  Update 'observed'
(the merged best-of-rounds CI value the ceiling was sized against) and
'set' when you do.  Ceilings sit well above observed values (roughly
+60%) because ubuntu-latest runners vary run to run; the relative gate
handles single-release moves, this file only caps the compounding.
Values are the metric's own unit: seconds, except mem.* in MB.
'proposed' below is NOT read by compare.py (it loads 'budgets' only).
It is where a ceiling waits out the ritual: a metric added this cycle
has no merged best-of-rounds CI value to size a ceiling against, and
an ubuntu-latest number is not a local one.  Move an entry into
'budgets' once one release has published an 'observed' value for it,
filling in 'observed' and 'set' at the same time.  The 'local' figures
recorded here are the developer-machine measurements the proposals were
derived from (max ~= 1.7x local, the same headroom the armed ceilings
carry) and exist only to make the later sizing decision auditable.  They
were taken on the post-audit tree, so they already price in the fixes.
config.parse_yaml_3k is there for more than drift: it catches a return
of the quadratic Seq validation, which cost 6.27s locally at 3k jobs
against 1.18s linear.  Its 2.0s ceiling is the usual ~1.7x of the local
figure and sits far under that 6.27s, so the absolute check fires on a
reintroduction even if the relative gate is waived.  Raising it past
~3s gives that up, so say why in the commit message if you ever do.
